quotes.text: As AI continues to play a larger role in our modern world, it’s critical that AI services are not biased and serve everyone fairly. [...] We had an important discussion about the need for AI policies that prevent discrimination and do not leave behind our Latino communities.
I’ve had students tell me, ‘Stop AI,’ and I say, ‘You want me to stop Google? You want me to stop you having access to Google’?

Great to join @sagaftra @WGAWest & labor allies at the picket this morning in front of Amazon Studios. 
  
#AMPTP MUST come to the table & bargain for a contract with fair pay & benefits that protects workers & prevents AI from taking their jobs. https://t.co/N2VrcCYkYs

Great to see @sagaftra has reached a tentative deal with the major studios to end the historic 118-day strike.

This deal includes pay raises & AI protections - a great win for the workers & another win for unions!

Congrats to everyone who held the line and stayed #UnionStrong! https://t.co/Ybt3V5Nkld

Was in the Bay Area last week to talk AI w/ @Samsung_RA & @intuit. Had a great conversation w/ #Samsung Pres. Wanil Roh & his team on their AI work for their devices & met w/ #Intuit to discuss their use of AI as a tool to help small businesses & individuals manage their finances. 

Spoke with both companies about the need for companies to assist underserved communities with access & education so they can benefit from the technology and not be left behind.

This is why Congress needs to regulate AI.
 
The industry has asked for guardrails.
 
Bad actors can abuse the technology & in the lead up to November’s election, the potential for the spread of mis- and disinformation using AI is very real and could have big consequences. https://t.co/pphnMjZnxI

Despite impressive advances, I am concerned about letting the fast-growing AI industry go unchecked, especially in critical areas like emergency communications. [...] If House Republicans' reconciliation bill becomes law, States will lose the ability to enforce new AI regulations for 10 years.
AI can help bridge those gaps, translating weather alerts or 911 calls in real time. But if we are not careful, errors and delays in translation could cost lives.
the use of AI can reduce workloads and improve eﬃciency in our healthcare system, but it can also make mistakes.

AI can transform the care that millions of Americans receive. With the rapid developments in AI technology, we now have the capability to do more, provide better care, and close the health care disparities that we often see in our underserved and minority communities. But that also means that our next generation of doctors and providers must be knowledgeable in how to best use this technology.

As artificial intelligence becomes more common in our workplaces, online spaces, and daily routines, people deserve clear, accessible information about how these technologies work. [...] This legislation will ensure consumers are better informed, better protected, and better prepared to navigate a rapidly changing digital landscape.

Profit should never come before American families, which is why the House just passed the Ratepayer Protection Act. This bill is a first step to ensure data center developers rightfully bear the higher electricity costs that come with the construction of these data centers — NOT families and small businesses. [...] America can lead in AI and innovation, but it must do so safely and without sacrificing the health of our families.
